sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Superpowers is a set of skills that gives AI coding agents a disciplined software development process. Once installed, your agent brainstorms the design with you, writes a step-by-step plan, builds it with tests first and reviews its own work.
sixtySeconds.problem: Coding agents tend to jump straight into writing code without understanding what you want, skip tests, and drift from the plan. Superpowers makes them ask questions first, plan in small tasks and follow test-driven development.
whoFor: Developers using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini CLI
People who want their agent to plan before coding
Teams that want agents to follow TDD and code review
Anyone running long autonomous agent sessions
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want a ready-made, opinionated workflow for your coding agent rather than writing your own prompts and rules. It is strict on purpose, for example it deletes code written before tests.
requirements: A supported coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, OpenCode and others)
A git repository to work in

overview: Superpowers is built from composable skills that trigger automatically. When you start building something, the agent first asks what you're really trying to do, shows the design back to you in short chunks, and only then writes an implementation plan broken into 2 to 5 minute tasks.

After you approve, it creates an isolated git worktree and works through the plan, either with a fresh subagent per task plus a review after each, or inline with one final review. Test-driven development is enforced: write a failing test, watch it fail, then write the code.

It installs separately for each agent you use, through official plugin marketplaces for Claude Code, Codex and Grok, or with each tool's own extension command. It is made by Jesse Vincent and Prime Radiant.

features.title: Brainstorming first
features.body: The agent asks questions and confirms the design before writing code.

features.title: Bite-sized plans
features.body: Work is split into small tasks with exact file paths and verification steps.

features.title: Test-driven development
features.body: Enforces red, green, refactor for every change.

features.title: Subagent-driven development
features.body: Fresh subagents handle each task, with a review after each one.

features.title: Code review and debugging skills
features.body: Includes systematic debugging, review and verification skills.

features.title: Works across agents
features.body: Installs into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI and more.

strengths: Skills trigger automatically, no special commands needed
Lets agents work for long stretches without drifting
Available in several official plugin marketplaces
limitations: Opinionated workflow may feel heavy for tiny changes
Must be installed separately for each agent you use
Longer sessions can use more tokens

tutorial.title: Build a feature with the Superpowers workflow
tutorial.useCase: Have your coding agent design, plan and build a small feature with tests.

steps.title: Describe what you want to build
steps.body: The brainstorming skill asks questions and plays its understanding back for you to correct.

steps.title: Approve the design
steps.body: The agent creates a git worktree and writes a plan of small tasks.

steps.title: Say go
steps.body: It works through the plan with test-driven development and reviews between tasks.

steps.title: Finish the branch
steps.body: When tasks are done it verifies tests and offers to merge, open a PR, keep or discard the work.

tutorial.expected: A tested feature on its own branch, built from a plan you approved.

troubleshooting.problem: A skill fires when it shouldn't, or the agent ignores its plan
troubleshooting.solution: Ask your agent to figure out what went wrong with superpowers in this session. The diagnosing skill reads the transcript and reports what happened.

troubleshooting.problem: Superpowers isn't active in a second agent
troubleshooting.solution: Install it separately for each harness you use.
